cases.expected: External callers cannot obtain the SQL connection or arbitrary runtime transaction callback.
Existing event identity, metadata and body survive UPDATE, DELETE, UPSERT and REPLACE on configured Store connections and snapshots.
Public event append rejects reserved receipts and mismatched session, work, branch or project bindings, including an explicit main selector in the CLI and MCP.
Exact branch and session queries, including pagination, preserve each history without relabelling events.
Two live processes sharing one expected revision produce one session commit and one explicit revision conflict.
The losing process cannot claim the same work and branch after refreshing its revision; no orphan session is created.
Two live contenders for an expired claim create exactly one successor claim and record the reclaimed identity.
Explicit expiry rejects unexpired finite and indefinite claims without modifying them.
Expired claim reclamation affects only its selected work and branch; unrelated effective claims remain owned.
A different session cannot release another session claim, including across branches and projects.
Zero and overflowing TTLs cannot leave a session, claim, event or revision change.
Failure of a reclamation receipt rolls back claim expiry, new ownership and new session creation together.
Live processes on different branches can retain independent claims after explicit revision retry.
Switching the default branch does not move existing sessions, claims, checkpoints or events.
Implicit session selection stays within the selected branch and reports ambiguity; explicit identity filters remain observable.
Handoff rejects a different branch, preserves checkpoint ownership and transfers only a live claim within the same branch.
Resume requires the original current branch, preserves claim expiry and creates only one successor.
Session end and explicit interruption release only their own claims and preserve other branch sessions.
Closed branches reject new sessions, claims and generic events without modifying existing history.
Checkpoint selection and related evidence keep named branch ownership while permitting shared source facts.

completion: Every condition must execute under this contract. Concurrency cases must coordinate distinct live OS processes and inspect committed session/claim/event ownership. Compile-fail API checks and SQL fault fixtures are component evidence, not real agent collaboration or E4. Historical counts never satisfy this contract.

required_transport_supplement.expected: Explicit main and named branch selectors cannot be silently overridden by a bound session; CLI/MCP errors preserve persisted state.
